title: Experimental demonstration of scalable quantum blockchain with exponentially superior quantum communication complexity
authors: Feng Xie, Ming-Yang Li, Yongqiang Du, Chen-Xun Weng, Mingxuan Zhang, Xin Hua, Xiang Guan, Xin An, Jingzhe He, Xin Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, Xi Xiao, Hua-Lei Yin, Kejin Wei
abstract: To secure modern distributed digital infrastructures, quantum blockchains exploit quantum resources to achieve information-theoretic security and surpass the classical one-third fault-tolerance bound. However, existing high-fault-tolerant protocols face a fundamental scalability challenge: the blockchain trilemma imposes either exponential communication complexity or experimentally demanding multipartite entanglement. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable quantum blockchain protocol based on weak coherent states that achieves an exponential reduction in quantum communication complexity. The protocol employs a circular quantum Byzantine agreement mechanism that preserves information-theoretic security while avoiding multipartite entanglement. We implement this protocol on a photonic integrated circuit platform, realizing a six-node network over commercially available telecommunication infrastructure. Compared with previous schemes, the protocol requires less than 4% of the quantum communication resources. Leveraging this advantage, we further demonstrate a quantum-secured token exchange application achieving a throughput of 805.3 transactions per second with zero failures. These results establish a practical pathway toward scalable quantum blockchain.
summary: The paper presents an experimental demonstration of a scalable quantum blockchain protocol designed to overcome the inherent limitations of previous high-fault-tolerance schemes. By utilizing weak coherent states and a novel circular Quantum Byzantine Agreement mechanism, they significantly reduce communication complexity. This breakthrough enables practical, high-throughput quantum-secured applications like token exchanges on existing fiber infrastructure.
main_problem: Existing high-fault-tolerant quantum blockchain protocols face a scalability challenge, known as the 'blockchain trilemma,' requiring either exponential communication complexity or demanding multipartite entanglement.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrated a scalable quantum blockchain protocol that achieves an exponential reduction in quantum communication complexity while maintaining information-theoretic security.
method: They employed a circular Quantum Byzantine Agreement (QBA) mechanism based on weak coherent states, which avoids complex multipartite entanglement requirements.
model_or_system: The protocol was implemented on a photonic integrated circuit platform, successfully realizing a six-node network over commercially available telecommunication infrastructure to secure a token exchange application.
key_observables: Sustained throughput of 805.3 transactions per second with zero failures; less than 4% quantum communication resource usage compared to prior schemes.
important_parameters: The protocol scales as $O(N^2)$ for the semi-decentralized structure, and it is secure if at least two participants are honest ($N > f+1$).
main_assumptions: The system assumes a layered architecture integrating quantum consensus with application-layer smart contracts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the token exchange workflow, the hierarchical two-layer architecture (quantum consensus + application), and detailed comparisons of communication complexity vs. node count for different QBA protocols.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework by proposing the circular QBA protocol, demonstrates its implementation on a photonic platform, validates performance metrics like key rates and throughput, and applies it to a quantum-secured token exchange workflow.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete experimental validation of scaling solutions for distributed quantum computing primitives (like consensus), which is highly relevant for building practical quantum networks beyond simple QKD links.

FIG. 2. Intercity deployment of scalable quantum blockchain network. A star-topology metropolitan quantum network implemented in Nanning, China, consisting of five user nodes (S, R1-R4) and a central CA. Two user nodes, S and R1, and the certification authority (CA) are co-located in the School of Physical Science and Technology (SP). Two additional campus nodes, R2 and R3, are deployed in the School of Computer and Electronic Information (SC) and connected to the CA via an intermediate network. A remote user node is deployed at a metropolitan government information center (IC) is connected to the CA via the Guangxi University Network Center (NC) over commercial telecommunication fiber.

Figure 3b compares this scaling with existing high-fault- tolerance multi-party QBA protocols under identical adver- sarial assumptions. Owing to its fault-tolerance condition 𝑁> 𝑓+1, the circular QBA protocol remains secure provided that at least two participants are honest. Consequently, our five- node metropolitan network can tolerate up to three malicious nodes. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first experimental quantum blockchain system achieving tolerance against three malicious nodes, whereas previous demonstra- tions were limited to one or two malicious nodes [24, 27, 28].
